subject: Technical deep dive recap & next steps (latency/throughput SLOs)

Subject: Technical deep dive recap & next steps (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Alice & Bob,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really valuable conversation. Below is a quick recap of the pain points you shared, the goals we discussed, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I copied Ethan and Vivek to keep engineering in the loop.

Pain points / goals (call notes)
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak traffic windows (p99 spikes to 800–1,200ms).
- Throughput needs to support ~120 sustained QPS for short prompt paths, with bursts to 300 QPS during marketing events.
- Need consistency across multi-region deployment (primary us-west-2, DR us-east-1).
- Data residency & VPC-only networking; SOC2 + encryption at rest/transport required.
- Want to run a mid-sized model (3B–7B) for chat with some heavier re-rank jobs using 13B variants.

Key constraints / assumptions
- Typical request size: ~60 tokens in, ~80 tokens out (avg ~140 tokens).
- p99 targets are for end-to-end response latency (including network hop to our cluster if using Dedicated).
- Short prompt chat path is the immediate priority; batch/rerank can tolerate higher latency.

Redwood recommendations (high level)
- Suggested SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 240ms for short-chat path at baseline load; target p99 < 350ms under 2x burst.
- Throughput sizing: baseline cluster to sustain 120 QPS with 1k-token context assumed; provide autoscaling headroom to 300 QPS bursts.
- Model variants: primary production on a 7B quantized model (4-bit) for cost/latency balance; reserve a 13B variant for rerank/long-context queries.
- Deployment topology: Dedicated VPC deployment in us-west-2 with a warm pool of GPU nodes + cross-region failover to us-east-1. Consider lightweight hosted fallback for short outages.
- Caching: Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts and cold-start reduction; we can pre-warm hot KV entries for common flows.

Attachments I shared
- redwood_slo_proposal.pdf — draft SLO targets and sizing rationale
- deployment_topology_sketch.png — recommended VPC & routing layout
- acme_network_requirements.xlsx — list of network ACLs and ports we’ll need for connectivity tests

Open questions / items for ACME
1) Can you share target 95th/99th percentile request size distribution and expected peak burst schedule (dates and duration)?
2) Any constraints on GPU families (we can propose H100/A100/Trn configs) or cloud partners?
3) Are you planning to do any fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented workflows that will increase context size?

Next steps
- I’ll send the SLO proposal and topology sketch attached (today).
- Let’s schedule a 60-minute technical workshop with your infra team so Ethan and Vivek can walk through network and capacity details — propose Wed 2027-05-20 10:00 PT.
- If you can share the distribution requested in (1) above before the workshop, we’ll bring a sizing runbook and concrete node counts.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — quick answers and more detail so we can prepare the workshop materials: 

Quantization & tail behavior
- Yes, Redwood supports int4/4-bit quantization for many open-architecture models we verify. For the 7B chat model we recommend Q4_0 or Q4_K_M variants — in our internal benchmarks these reduce memory and improve throughput with minimal accuracy regression.
- Tail latency impact: quantized models generally reduce per-token compute and improve p50/p95; p99 tail is still often dominated by queuing and batching strategy. We’ll design batching to prefer low-latency paths for short-chat (e.g., continuous batching with per-route latency caps).

13B rerank footprint (approx)
- For 13B quantized (4-bit) optimized on GPU: expect ~1 x H100 or 2 x A100 (40GB) per hot replica for low-latency single-node serving. If you prefer fewer GPUs we can use model sharding, which increases p99 slightly.

Sizing notes & assumptions we’ll use for the workshop
- Assume avg sequence length 140 tokens and 1k-context headroom for some flows.
- Baseline cluster to hit 120 QPS: ~6–8 hot replicas of the 7B quantized model (depends on exact GPU family and batching window).
- Autoscaling to support 300 QPS bursts: add a warm pool of 6–10 additional nodes to avoid cold-start latency.

Deployment topology (summary)
- Dedicated VPC in us-west-2 with an internal load-balancer routing to a GPU pool (hot replicas + warm pool).
- Cross-region DR in us-east-1 with asynchronous KV replication and a failover policy (we’ll coordinate RTO expectations).
- Optional: lightweight hosted fallback for short outages (will serve short-chat on a hosted instance with slightly relaxed SLOs).

What we’ll bring to the workshop
- Concrete node counts and cost estimates for H100 vs A100 configurations.
- Network connectivity checklist and test plan (we’ll run a handshake test during the workshop).
- A quick demo of warm-pool pre-warm and observed p99 improvements on similar workloads.

I’ll attach the SLO proposal and topology sketch to the calendar invite. Ethan/Vivek — feel free to add any infrastructure items you want addressed.

Thanks,
Marissa
